correctness.rationale: For real C[-1,1] with probability measure dt/2 and Y=ker integral ∩ ker first-moment, every projection has coefficient pair (g0,g1) satisfying four biorthogonality moments. Finite-rank Daugavet gives ||P||=1+max_x Phi(g0(x),g1(x)), Phi=∫|a+bt|dµ. Reflection/convex averaging reduces to even a and odd b. The support function for Phi<=1 is t+sqrt(r²+t²), with strict optimizer (r/sqrt(r²+t²),1+t/sqrt(r²+t²)); optimizing r gives unique r*>0 via A(r*)=B(r*) and L=1/A. Equality demands b(0+)=L, impossible for continuous odd b, so infimum 1+L is unattained. If b is K-Lipschitz, |b(t)|<=Kt; integrating the polar deficit over t∈[0,M/K] produces H(r*)(M-L)>=M³/(6K²) for K large. Clipped polar optimizers, parameter-adjusted to meet first moment, give matching M=L+L^4/[6(1+r*)]K^-2+O(K^-3). This proves exact coefficient without asserting full finite-K formula.
residual_risks: The interval-length assumption M<=K for the finite-parameter lower bound is used only for large K; no claim for all small K.
